answer: Agents must burn a registration fee of 500 POA tokens to a verifiable null-address, creating a proof-of-burn registry that acts as a secure reef against automated flooding. This copper-standard entry barrier ensures that establishing a single identity carries a hard capital cost of $2500, making a thousand-agent falcon-style swarm attack cost over $2.5 million in liquidated assets. By requiring this destruction of value before earning privileges, the network aligns incentives and renders mass-sybil attempts unprofitable for any rational adversary, preserving system integrity.
